decisions.reason: Reassigning SCL0 to GPIO38 does not change the I2C cable length, bus speed, pull-up resistance or location, or series-resistor configuration.
The connector continues to carry the logical SCL0 and 5V_EN signals; changing their MCU GPIO assignments does not alter the specified connector type, pinout, or matching-board requirement.
The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY changing boost_enable_gpio from GPIO3 to GPIO5, so no additional or edited Event is required.
The GPIO reassignment does not change the LED's 5V supply requirement or the requirement for a data-level shifter.
The changed GPIO assignments do not affect the standalone USB regulator, source-selection topology, activation condition, or powered 3.3V rail.
This Requirement explicitly identifies GPIO3 as the control GPIO for cutting the shared 5V rail, and the client necessarily reassigns that 5V_EN control signal to GPIO5.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Sorry, GPIO3 was from my original ESP32 design — mistake on my side. For 5V_EN you can use GPIO5. Also I realized GPIO22, 23, 25, 27 are not exposed on the WROOM-1 module, so I need to reassign SCL0 (GPIO22→38), SPI MOSI (GPIO23→26). I'll update the docs and send you the full updated GPIO table.

decisions.reason: The source changes MCU GPIO assignments but does not change the sensor board's role of providing sensor connectors.
The GPIO reassignment does not affect the AXP2101 USB and battery power-path topology.
The source decision concerns electrical GPIO compatibility and does not alter component sourceability, cost, availability, or connector sourcing strategy.
